title: Solo dev, launching on Epic tonight: how I used AI as one tool among many for a first-person Halloween tower defence
author: maxhit_studios
selftext:
I'm James, a solo developer in Melbourne. My game Ravenspire is on itch now, with a free demo, and goes live on the Epic Games Store at 3:00 AM Melbourne time on 13 November. It's US$2.99.

It's a first-person gothic tower defence game. You play the Arcanist, holding a castle overnight against skeletons, ghouls, wraiths and werewolves, while building towers and fighting on the walls with your staff.

How AI fit in: I used it as one tool among many, not as the thing that made the game. It helped with some of the art, 3D models, music and in-game text. Everything else was done the usual way: the design, the level layout, the balancing, putting it all together in the engine, and the testing. As one person, the biggest gain was speed in the early art and audio passes, which left me more time for the gameplay and the polish.

What I learned: AI output is a starting point. It still took a lot of editing, rejected attempts and hand fixes to make everything feel like one game rather than a pile of assets. The hard part was getting it all consistent.

Free demo: [https://maxhitstudios.itch.io/ravenspire](https://maxhitstudios.itch.io/ravenspire)

Epic: [https://store.epicgames.com/p/ravenspire-fcadb2](https://store.epicgames.com/p/ravenspire-fcadb2)

Happy to answer questions about the process.
